narrative.overview:
Fork looks like a cookbook that has been cooked from: cream paper, a serif for the recipe names, and a cook's notes in the margin. The notes are the product. Version numbers, bylines, dates and gram weights are set in a monospace face, the way a pencil annotation differs from the printed page, so a reader always knows which marks are the recipe and which are its history. Everything else recedes: one dark surface (the espresso navbar), one text accent (clay), one action colour (marigold).

Density is editorial rather than app-like. Body text sits at 16px with generous leading, the page has one 1200px column with 24px gutters (18px on a phone), and recipe cards are content on the paper, not tiles. Surfaces separate by a step in tone, never by shadow. The system is warm (paper, clay, marigold), exact (tabular figures, one focus ring, 8px rhythm) and simple (three faces doing three jobs, two button styles, one chip). Its colour should be decently vibrant: the owner finds the current clay and marigold a little dull and wants more life in them, short of anything neon.

Confirmed rejections: no gradients, no glass, no shadows on resting elements, no colour other than clay and marigold outside the diff.
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper ground with one espresso bar; nothing else is dark.
Bitter for names and titles, Source Sans 3 for everything read, JetBrains Mono for every mark that is history or measurement.
Clay is the only coloured text; marigold is the only fill.
Depth is tonal: paper, lifted paper, clay tint, espresso.
Version chips, bylines and diffs are first-class marks, set in mono.

rules.name: The Clay Is Text Rule
rules.body: Clay never fills a shape. It colours titles, links and version marks. Its hover is ink.

rules.name: The Pencil Rule
rules.body: Anything that is history or measurement (version number, byline, date, fork count, grams, diff text) is set in JetBrains Mono. Anything that is the recipe (title, description, ingredients, steps) is not. The reader tells the two apart by face alone.

rules.name: The One Clay Line Rule
rules.body: Clay running text is the h1 and links. Headings below h1 are ink.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. A shadow appears only on something that truly floats above the page: a dialog, a menu.

dos: set every version number, byline, date, count and gram weight in JetBrains Mono.
keep clay for titles, links and version marks, and marigold for the one action.
separate surfaces with a tone step or a 1px rule; reserve shadows for dialogs.
keep body text at 16px, ink, with a measure under about 72 characters.
compose desktop and iPad first; give the phone its own crop and order without reshaping the desktop.
hold the layout when a recipe has no photo; the clay-tint panel is the fallback.
donts: add a second dark surface, a gradient, a blur or a glow.
fill anything with clay, or colour text marigold.
put a shadow on a card, strip or button at rest.
invent proof: no ratings, counts, testimonials or press.
let the version UI crowd the recipe; where it harms reading, reduce it on that surface rather than the whole system.
